content.text:
**Recommendation: Sentry**, unless your team is mostly native mobile, in which case Bugsnag is the stronger pick. Rollbar is a reasonable option but doesn't win on any axis that matters most for a 10-person team.

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core strength** | Broadest product: errors, tracing, session replay, profiling, uptime, logs | Solid error grouping, deploy tracking, RQL search | Stability scores, release health, strong mobile SDKs |
| **SDK coverage** | Very wide (web, backend, mobile, games, most languages) | Wide, with fewer first-party integrations | Strong for web and mobile; a few backend gaps |
| **Free tier** | Generous, enough to start with a small team | Small (about 5k events/month) | Small, limited to a few seats |
| **Performance / replay** | Included in the platform, with separate usage-based quotas | Limited compared to Sentry | Limited; performance is a secondary product |
| **Pricing model** | Usage-based across several products; spend can rise with traffic spikes unless you set spike protection and quotas | Per-event tiers, with seat limits on some plans | Per-event tiers, with seat limits and mobile-focused plans |
| **Self-hosting** | Yes (open source) | No | No |
| **Integrations** | Broad: GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, PagerDuty, and more | Good core integrations | Good core integrations |

**Why Sentry for this team:**
- It covers error tracking today and tracing or session replay later, so you won't need a second tool when you want to debug performance.
- Its free tier and team plan let you start cheaply and grow.
- Its integrations with GitHub and Slack make it easy to route errors to the people who will fix them.
- Self-hosting is available if you ever need to keep data in-house.

**When I'd choose differently:**
- **Bugsnag** if most of your code is native iOS or Android and you care most about stability and crash-free-session metrics.
- **Rollbar** if your team already uses it or you prefer its grouping and search model. Otherwise I wouldn't pick it fresh.

**Before you commit:**
- Pricing for all three changes often, and I may be out of date. Check current pricing pages, and estimate your monthly event volume to compare real costs.
- Set spend caps or spike protection on whichever you choose.
- If you tell me your stack (languages, web vs. mobile) and rough event volume, I can narrow this to a specific plan.
